Commonwealth-MCP

An MCP server that lets AI assistants look things up in Virginia’s government records, and tells you which government system each answer came from.

What this is → Try it in your browser

What this is

↑ ↓

The problem

Virginia has 133 counties and independent cities, and each one publishes its records its own way. Different software, different field names, different rules about what you are allowed to do with the data. Some publish a clean API. Some publish a map you can only look at.

So anyone who wants to answer a question like “how is this parcel zoned” has to work out, for every locality separately, where that answer lives and whether they are allowed to fetch it. Every project does that work again from scratch.

What MCP is

The Model Context Protocol is a standard way to give an AI assistant access to an outside system. You run a small server, point the assistant at it, and the assistant can call the things that server offers. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and others all speak it.

What this project does

It does the per-locality work once, writes down what it learned, and exposes the result as an MCP server. An assistant connected to it can ask a plain question and get a structured answer back.

Most of the care goes into what comes back with the answer: which government system produced it, when it was fetched, and what was not checked. A zoning district read off a county map layer is screening evidence; the adopted ordinance is what governs. The answer states that rather than leaving you to assume a lookup settles it.

Read-only. It fetches published public records and submits nothing.

What you can ask

↑ ↓

These are the four questions it can answer today.

“Which local government covers this spot?”

You get the county or independent city. If the spot is in a town, you get the town as well, because both govern that ground. Ask by name and hit one that matches two places, and you get both to choose between.

“What is the parcel with this ID, or at this point on the map?”

The assessor’s record for that parcel. Where a county publishes its own and the state publishes one too, you get both answers rather than a guess about which is right. Street addresses do not work yet, so a parcel is found by its ID or by coordinates.

“How is this parcel zoned?”

The zoning district from the county’s own map layer. This is a screening answer. The adopted ordinance is what governs, and the answer says so every time.

“What does § 18.2-57 of the Code of Virginia say?”

You get the text of that section, taken from the state’s own site, with a link to the live page.

Answers also carry the date they were fetched. And if nothing was found, you are told which kind of nothing: the records were searched and came back empty, or there is no source registered for that place at all. Most systems show the same blank screen for both.

Government sources

Places

Virginia is unusually hard to get right. Its 38 independent cities are not inside any county, including the counties they share a name with, and towns sit inside counties so both govern the same ground. These are the pairs that catch systems out:

Skills

A skill bundles several tool calls into one workflow. None are built yet. There is not enough coverage for one to be worth having, and a skill that only chains two tools together adds nothing a model cannot already do.

Install it

↑

From the repo root. The tests run offline, replaying recorded government responses.

uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e . --group dev
.venv/bin/commonwealth doctor --live
.venv/bin/commonwealth tools call geo.find_zoning \
  --args '{"jurisdiction": "Fairfax County", "pin": "0102 14  0231"}'
.venv/bin/commonwealth serve

That zoning answer is screening evidence, with the caveat attached to it — see what you can ask.

Or run an example first

Four short scripts in the repo, each a real question with a printed answer. They replay recorded government responses by default, so a first run cannot fail on a network or a service being down.

python examples/whose_government.py          # recorded responses
python examples/whose_government.py --live   # the real services

whose_government.py asks about a mailing address whose city is not its government. screen_a_parcel.py walks a property question from PIN to zoning to buildings to monitored sites. what_is_covered.py shows what an empty answer means here. two_sources_disagree.py shows two official sources describing one road differently.
